title: Getting a Word In When Senior Colleagues Present
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article offers a tactical approach for colleagues who struggle to contribute when presenting alongside a dominant, highly articulate coworker. Rather than trying to interrupt or slow the other person down, it recommends starting with visible agreement, nods and affirming words, then escalating to declarative statements that others will register as support. Once established as an engaged voice, the piece suggests, it becomes easier to add a genuine point, example, or question without the interjection feeling disruptive. It closes by framing this as a repeatable cycle: agree, then contribute, then repeat.
points: Offers a step-by-step tactic for gaining airtime alongside a dominant co-presenter
Recommends starting with visible agreement before escalating to real contributions
Explains why agreement-based entry points feel less disruptive than interruption
Frames the approach as a repeatable cycle rather than a one-time move
quotes: Those brilliant, articulate, and outspoken colleagues present a massive challenge for those who present with them.
The enthusiasm with which they compel others to yield to their views is like a locomotive.
The best initial way in is to make it clear that you are in agreement with what is being said or presented.
Once you’re in, even in a supporting voice, you now have the ability to make a stronger statement or to ask a question.
Realizing after the presentation that you didn’t say much or add any value is an empty feeling, even when the presentation is well received.
You owe it to everyone to find a way to get heard. Agreement is the path forward.
